relevance_note: The paper describes eight HA20 patients with TNFAIP3 variants from three Chinese families individually: 'we report eight patients with HA20 from three unrelated families in China'.
method_note: Read in full by hand; a short Python script (scratch dir) assembled the JSON and built Table 1 row-prefix spans, checked against the table. Table 1 has no label column (first column is the pedigree number); patients are matched to rows by content: row 1 = P1 (onset 18, diagnosis 28), rows 2-4 = mother IV:14 and sisters V:22, V:26 (the three rows are identical, so values do not depend on which row is whose), row 5 = IV:1 of Family 2 (onset 9, diagnosis 12; text: 13-year-old, onset age nine), row 6 = P2 (15/35), row 7 = P3 (M, 40), row 8 = IV:1 of Family 3 (F, 8/10). Table legend defines '+, postive; -, negative.'; the cells print an en dash '–', which I read as the legend's '-' and recorded as excluded with the legend quoted. Labels: P1-P3 are the paper's patient labels; IV:1 and III:3 each name people in two families, so the daughters are 'IV:1 (Family 2)' / 'IV:1 (Family 3)' and the Family 2 cousin is 'III:3 (Family 2)' (P3's pedigree number is also III:3). Contradictions in the paper: (1) P1 genital ulcers: text 'recurrent oral and genital ulcers from the age of 22' and Discussion vs Table 1 Genital ulcers '–' (both rows emitted; checklist not reported). (2) Fever in Family 2: text says P2 was 'without recurrent fever' and the daughter had 'recurrent fever', but Table 1 shows Fever '+' for P2's row and '–' for the daughter's row (both rows emitted for each; checklist recurrent fever not reported for both). (3) P3 autoantibodies: positive anti-TG and anti-TPO (text and Table 1) vs 'autoantibodies were all normal' (both emitted; checklist not reported). (4) P3 age at onset: text 'recurrent oral ulcers since the age of 10' vs Table 1 onset 15; individual age_at_onset left not reported, the text onset kept on the oral-ulcer feature row. (5) A547T pathogenicity: Abstract 'validated to be pathogenic' vs Discussion 'accurate pathogenic significance of A547T was indeed unknown'; both quoted. Other notes: P3's Henoch-Schonlein purpura at 30 recorded as vasculitis observed, while Table 1 Skin lesions '–' kept as excluded. P2's moderate anemia is not stated to be autoimmune, so checklist cytopenia (autoimmune) left not reported. Normal whole investigations (biochemistry panel, urine analysis, chest CT, Ig) recorded as written (D-27); normal CBC recorded as excluding cytopenia. Uveitis-only or arthritis-only absences did not exclude the composite checklist items; 'no ocular symptoms' did not exclude uveitis (P1 had asymptomatic old uveitis). Post-treatment absences (P1, IV:1 Family 2) were not recorded as features. Scope: the father IV:13 (no symptoms; source of P1's paternal NOD2 variant) is included as a described relative; his checklist is left not reported despite 'had no symptoms'. Family 2 aunt II:3 and cousins III:3, III:4 (affected; refused gene testing) and Family 3 II:4 and late I:4 (affected, untested) are included without variant rows. Not included: P1's grandparents III:2/III:3 (only stated to be cousins; grandparental consanguinity, so consanguinity not recorded for anyone), and cousin V:10 and 'her son' VI:7 with G6PD deficiency (not HA20-affected or tested). Variants: P1's NOD2 and G6PD variants recorded because attributed to her; NOD2 inheritance 'inherited paternal' from 'a paternal heterozygous ... variant'. Family 1 relatives' zygosity left not reported (only a family-level figure legend says heterozygous); their cDNA/protein from Table 1, transcript NM_006290 from the Table 1 header (P1 text gives NM_006290.4). Sisters V:22/V:26 recorded as inherited maternal because their (and P1's) mother IV:14 carries A547T. The literature review (126 patients from 35 articles) is reported only at group level; no previously published individuals are described, so none were extracted.
